which human organ produces insulin?: The pancreas makes insulin, a hormone that helps cells take up sugar from the blood. When it doesn't work properly, diabetes can result.
in the treatment of what serious disease: Gold-198 is a radioactive isotope that has been used in cancer treatment, for example as small implanted seeds that deliver radiation to a tumor. It decays quickly, so its effect is short-lived.
how often can a healthy adult donate blo: In the United States, a healthy adult can donate whole blood about every 8 weeks (56 days). The wait gives the body time to replace the red blood cells and iron.
according to some studies, lycopene, whi: Lycopene, the red pigment in tomatoes, is an antioxidant that has been linked in some studies to a lower risk of certain cancers, particularly prostate cancer. The evidence is mixed, so it's not a proven preventive.
animal liver is very rich in this health: Liver is a very rich source of iron and vitamin A, which is why it has long been recommended for people with anemia. Too much vitamin A can be harmful, so it is best eaten in moderation.
what vitamin is the garden strawberry a: Strawberries are an excellent source of vitamin C, with a cup providing more than most people's daily needs. They also have fiber and antioxidants.
paprika, and chili peppers in general, a: Chili peppers and paprika are high in vitamin C, and a single red chili has more than an orange by weight. Vitamin C helps the body make collagen and fight infection.
what vitamin are lychee fruits rich in?: Lychees are rich in vitamin C, with a handful providing much of a day's needs. The fruit originated in southern China.
rose hips, the fruit of the rose plant,: Rose hips, the small red fruit of the rose plant, are one of the richest plant sources of vitamin C. In World War II, Britain made rose hip syrup to replace imported citrus fruit.
what important vitamin does asparagus co: Asparagus is a good source of vitamin B9, or folate, which the body needs to make DNA and new cells. It is especially important during pregnancy.
sigmund freud, who was a heavy cigar smo: Sigmund Freud smoked about 20 cigars a day, and he developed cancer of the mouth and jaw, which led to dozens of operations before he died in 1939. He kept smoking despite the warnings of his doctors.
the term encephalon, defined as the brai: "Encephalon" comes from a Greek phrase meaning "in the head", from en (in) and kephalē (head). It's another word for the brain, and it's why we have the word "encephalitis".
because of the substance present in thes: Teeth are covered with enamel, the hardest substance in the body, made mostly of the mineral hydroxyapatite. This is why teeth often survive for centuries after other tissues have decayed.
which of the following disease does prop: Propecia (finasteride) is used to treat male pattern hair loss. It blocks the conversion of testosterone to DHT, a hormone that shrinks hair follicles.
extract from the periwinkle plant is one: The Madagascar periwinkle is the source of vincristine and vinblastine, drugs used to treat cancers such as leukemia and Hodgkin lymphoma. The discovery of their power helped to spark interest in plants as sources of medicine.
in 1993 the scottish hotel-owner campbel: In 1993, hotel owner Campbell Aird became the first person to be fitted with a bionic arm, a myoelectric prosthetic developed in Scotland. It's controlled by electrical signals from the wearer's muscles.
the fallopian tubes are part of this sys: The Fallopian tubes are part of the female reproductive system, linking the ovaries to the uterus. Eggs travel through them, and fertilization usually happens there.
nephrectomy is a surgical removal of whi: A nephrectomy is the surgical removal of a kidney, a procedure used for cancer, severe injury or donation. People can live a healthy life with one kidney.
one type of hair on the human body is ca: Vellus hair is the fine, short, light "peach fuzz" that covers most of the body, except the palms and soles. It helps regulate body temperature.
which of the following is true about the: Vitamin B5 (pantothenic acid) is found in almost all foods, and its name comes from a Greek word meaning "from everywhere". Because of this, a true deficiency is rare.
vitamin b12 is a set of complex chemical: Only bacteria and archaea, a type of microbe, can make vitamin B12. Animals get it from eating other animals or from the bacteria in their food, which is why vegans often need supplements.
which of the following is a water solubl: Vitamin B2, also called riboflavin, is a water-soluble vitamin that helps the body use energy from food. It is found in milk, eggs and leafy greens.
the lack of this vitamin may cause sebor: A lack of vitamin B6 can cause skin problems like seborrheic dermatitis (an itchy, flaky rash) as well as irritability and anemia. It's found in fish, poultry, bananas and potatoes.
which of these would not cause a muscle: Common triggers for muscle cramps include dehydration, low levels of electrolytes like potassium or magnesium, overexertion and poor circulation. Body weight by itself isn't a direct cause.
what is the approximate surface of the s: An adult's skin covers about 1.5 to 2 square meters, making it the body's largest organ. It protects against germs, regulates temperature and gives us the sense of touch.
an overdose of what vitamin can cause di: Very high doses of vitamin B5 (pantothenic acid) can cause diarrhea and an upset stomach. It's normally harmless at the levels found in food.
Niacin is another name for vitamin B3. A lack of it causes pellagra, a disease with skin, digestive and mental symptoms.
what is the main symptom of the uncommon: In methemoglobinemia, the blood has too much methemoglobin, a form of hemoglobin that cannot carry oxygen well. The result is a bluish or grayish skin color.
which scientist discovered that blood co: Dr. Charles Drew found that blood plasma could be separated from red cells and stored longer, which made large-scale blood banks possible. His work saved many lives during World War II.
scientists have proved that one of the h: Diets high in sugar are linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes and inflammation, and some studies suggest they can weaken immune responses. Researchers are still working out the details.
named after a 19th century british surge: Bowman's capsule is a cup-shaped structure in each of the kidney's filtering units (nephrons), where blood is first filtered. It was named after the English surgeon Sir William Bowman, who described it in the 1840s.
what chemical is added to table salt in: Fluoride, usually in the form of sodium fluoride, is added to salt in some countries, including Switzerland, Germany and France. It strengthens tooth enamel and helps prevent cavities.
this term, denoting an internal organ, a: "Liver" is both the large organ that filters blood and makes bile, and the name of a brownish-gray color. The color is named after the organ's reddish-brown look.
what disease do the following famous peo: All of these famous people had diabetes. The disease affects how the body handles blood sugar, and today it is far more common than in their time.
this medical term refers to a disease-ca: A prion is an infectious protein that has no DNA or RNA. Prions cause diseases such as mad cow disease and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, and Stanley Prusiner won a Nobel Prize in 1997 for discovering them.
although natural, this food contains mor: Honey has been used as a food and medicine since ancient times, including in ancient Egypt. A tablespoon has more calories than a tablespoon of table sugar, but it contains small amounts of other compounds.
how does chocolate affect blood choleste: Research on chocolate and cholesterol is mixed: dark chocolate's flavanols may modestly improve some cholesterol markers, but chocolate also contains saturated fat and sugar. Moderation is the usual advice.
besides containing vitamin e, this fruit: Mangoes contain vitamin E, vitamin C and carotenoids such as beta-carotene, which the body turns into vitamin A. They help keep skin and eyes healthy.
bitter melon, or bitter gourd, has been: Bitter melon has been used in traditional medicine across Asia and Latin America to treat illnesses including malaria, and also diabetes. Scientific evidence for such uses is limited.
stinging nettle has a large number of me: Fresh stinging nettle is rich in vitamin K, which the body needs for blood to clot properly. Cooking removes the sting.
the consumption of blood oranges prevent: Blood oranges get their red color from anthocyanins, powerful antioxidants that may help protect the eyes. They also contain vitamin C, but no food can guarantee that you won't develop cataracts.
high consumption of meat protein deprive: Calcium is the main mineral in bones, and a lack of it over time, along with a lack of vitamin D, can lead to osteoporosis, a disease that makes bones brittle. Weight-bearing exercise also helps protect them.
what disease is named after the main cha: Syphilis got its name from Syphilus, a shepherd in an epic poem published in 1530 by the Italian physician Girolamo Fracastoro. In the poem, Syphilus is cursed with the disease.
what dangerous disease did queen elizabe: Queen Elizabeth I caught smallpox in October 1562 and nearly died, but she recovered. She was left with some scarring, and it is said that she wore heavy makeup afterward.
in preparation for a blood test, the lab: NPO is short for the Latin "nil per os", meaning "nothing by mouth". It means no food or drink, often before surgery or certain blood tests.
leukemia is a disease harming this bodil: Leukemia is a cancer of the blood-forming tissues, such as the bone marrow, and it affects the white blood cells that are a key part of the immune system. It is the most common childhood cancer.
tee is a good anti-stress therapy. flavo: Tea contains flavonoids, antioxidants that may help protect the heart by keeping LDL cholesterol from oxidizing and by helping blood vessels to function well. Studies generally support a modest benefit.
tea could reduce the risk for gastric, e: Some studies suggest the polyphenols in tea may lower the risk of certain cancers, including gastric, esophageal and skin cancers. The evidence is not conclusive, so tea isn't a substitute for medical advice.
you can reduce contact with your teeth w: Using a straw when drinking soda helps limit how long the sugary, acidic liquid is in contact with your teeth. Rinsing with water afterward also helps.
which of these organs has no known funct: The appendix was once thought to be useless, but it contains immune tissue and may serve as a reserve of helpful gut bacteria. Some people live a normal life without it.
these organs are very sensitive and ofte: The kidneys contain millions of tiny blood vessels that are easily damaged by high blood pressure and diabetes, the two leading causes of kidney failure. Controlling these conditions protects them.
which of these is best describes the cau: Parkinson's disease is caused by the loss of dopamine-producing nerve cells in a part of the brain called the substantia nigra. Dopamine is a neurotransmitter that helps control movement.
this disease had 7 pandemics and is stil: Cholera has caused seven pandemics since 1817, and the current one began in 1961. It spreads through water contaminated with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.
this organ contains many bacteria, which: The intestines hold trillions of bacteria. After death, the bacteria begin to break down the tissue, starting the decomposition process.
three of the following four disorders ar: "Manic depression", "bipolar disorder" and "manic-depressive illness" are all names for the same condition, which causes swings between high and low moods. "Maniac" is not the name of a disease.
what lobe in the brain is responsible fo: The left temporal lobe, especially the hippocampus, plays a key role in forming and retrieving verbal memories. Damage there can cause trouble remembering words and conversations.
this organ expands up to 500 times its n: During pregnancy, the uterus grows to about 500 times its normal size, from the size of a small pear to a large organ holding the baby. It returns to near its original size after birth.
what is the function of the thalamus, a: The thalamus is an egg-shaped relay center deep in the brain that passes sensory information, such as touch, sight and hearing, to the cortex. Smell is the exception.
which disease is treated by synthroid (l: Synthroid (levothyroxine) is a synthetic thyroid hormone used to treat hypothyroidism, a condition in which the thyroid gland doesn't make enough hormone. It is among the most commonly prescribed drugs.
despite its natural origins, this food i: Dried fruits are sticky and have concentrated sugars, so they cling to teeth and feed cavity-causing bacteria. Brushing or rinsing after eating them helps.
what marrow produces blood cells in the: Red bone marrow, found in flat bones like the hip and breastbone, produces red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. Yellow marrow, in the long bones, stores fat.
what is the building block of green plan: Dietary fiber is the part of plant foods that humans cannot digest, so it passes through the body mostly intact. It helps digestion and heart health.
approximately what percentage of humans: About 85% of people have Rh-positive blood, meaning they have the Rh factor protein on their red blood cells. The remaining 15% are Rh-negative.
what percentage of humans have type o bl: Type O is the most common blood type in many countries, with about 45% of people in the US having it, including O-positive and O-negative. O-negative is the universal donor type for red cells.
healthy people over 17 can donate what p: Platelet donors can give as often as every two weeks, much more often than whole-blood donors. Platelets help blood to clot and are in constant demand for cancer patients.
who was the first physician to demonstra: The Greek physician Galen showed in the 2nd century that arteries carry blood rather than air, which earlier doctors believed. His ideas remained influential until William Harvey described circulation in 1628.
in 1924 who was the german mathematician: In 1924, the German mathematician Felix Bernstein showed that the ABO blood types are inherited through three versions of one gene. His work explained patterns that had puzzled scientists for years.
this person developed the first system t: Charles Drew developed methods to process and store blood plasma and became the first director of the American Red Cross blood bank. He also resigned in protest when the Red Cross segregated blood by race.
which of the following is high in vitami: Sunflower seeds are one of the best sources of vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells. Almonds and wheat germ are also rich in it.
what is the male reproductive organ whic: The prostate gland makes a slightly alkaline fluid that is part of semen. It helps protect sperm in the acidic environment of the female reproductive tract.
identify the true statement regarding ca: Cardiac muscle, found only in the heart, is striated like skeletal muscle but works involuntarily. It contracts rhythmically and does not tire.
identify a true characteristic of the sm: Smooth muscle, found in the walls of organs such as the stomach and blood vessels, contracts slowly and involuntarily. It moves things such as food through the digestive tract.
what word denotes the ability of the mus: Conductivity is the ability of muscle to carry electrical impulses. Muscles also have excitability, contractility, extensibility and elasticity.
identify a true characteristic of skelet: Skeletal muscle is made of long, striped (striated) fibers and is under voluntary control. It attaches to bones with tendons and moves the skeleton.
what disease took many lives in russia,: Typhus, spread by body lice, killed hundreds of thousands in Russia, Poland, Romania and Serbia during and after World War I. Crowded, unsanitary conditions helped it spread.
electrooculography is a medical procedur: Electrooculography (EOG) measures the electrical potential between the front and back of the eye, using electrodes placed around it. It is used to study eye movements and retina function.
sigmoidoscopy is a medical examination o: A sigmoidoscopy examines the lower part of the large intestine, the rectum and the sigmoid colon, with a thin, flexible camera. It is used to screen for polyps and cancer.
uncontrolled hypertension (high blood pr: Uncontrolled high blood pressure can damage the heart, brain and kidneys, causing heart attack, stroke and kidney disease. It doesn't cause thyroid disease.
blood sugars are checked under 2 conditi: A post-prandial blood sugar test is done about two hours after a meal. It shows how well the body handles the sugar from food.
which of the following is a normal fasti: A normal fasting blood glucose level is below 100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L). Readings between 100 and 125 suggest prediabetes, and 126 or above on two tests suggests diabetes.
which of the following is a normal post-: A normal blood sugar two hours after eating is less than 140 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L). Higher readings suggest the body is not handling sugar well.
which of the following is least likely t: Tooth decay happens when bacteria in the mouth turn sugars and starches into acid that eats away at enamel. How often you eat sugary foods matters even more than how much.
an important supplement for pregnant wom: Vitamin B9 is also called folate, and its supplement form is folic acid. Taking it before and during early pregnancy helps prevent neural tube defects.
the vitamins from the b complex have man: B vitamins help the body turn food into energy and are central to cell metabolism. They also help make red blood cells and support the nervous system.
which of these is not among the systems: B vitamins mainly benefit the nervous system, the digestive system, the skin and the blood, but they aren't typically linked to the respiratory system. They are mostly water-soluble, so the body needs a regular supply.
vitamin b2 has which of these interestin: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) glows yellow-green under UV light, which is why vitamin-rich urine can look bright yellow. Its name comes from the Latin "flavus", meaning yellow.
niacin, also known as vitamin b3 or nico: The liver can make niacin from the amino acid tryptophan. That's why foods rich in tryptophan, like turkey and milk, help prevent niacin deficiency.
this vitamin of the b complex, popular a: Vitamin B7, biotin, is also called vitamin H, from the German words for "skin and hair". Some health organizations set no official daily value because deficiency is rare.
what kind of animal causes the parasitic: Dracunculiasis, or Guinea worm disease, is caused by a parasitic worm that people catch by drinking water containing tiny water fleas carrying its larvae. Cases have fallen from millions to only a handful per year thanks to eradication efforts.
where in the human body is the golgi org: The Golgi tendon organ is a sensor located in tendons, near where they attach to muscles. It detects tension and helps prevent muscles from being overloaded.
the so-called mcburneys point is located: McBurney's point is a spot on the lower right side of the abdomen, about two-thirds of the way from the navel to the hip bone. Tenderness there is a classic sign of appendicitis.
oxytocin is an important hormone for the: Oxytocin causes the uterus to contract during labor and triggers milk letdown during breastfeeding. It's also called the "love hormone" because it's linked to bonding.
vitamin a plays an important role in vis: Good sources of vitamin A include liver, eggs, dairy, and orange and green vegetables like carrots and spinach. Nuts and grains are not significant sources.
which of the following is not a heart va: The heart's four valves are the mitral, tricuspid, aortic and pulmonary valves. The carotid is an artery in the neck, not a heart valve.
how many types of blood vessels are ther: The main kinds of blood vessels are arteries, veins and capillaries, and smaller arterioles and venules are often counted separately, which makes four or five types. They would stretch about 60,000 miles if laid end to end.
on average, how much of a persons body w: Muscle makes up around 40% of an average person's body weight, though this varies with age, sex and fitness. Skeletal muscle is the main component.
how many muscles are in the human body?: The human body has roughly 600 to 650 skeletal muscles, depending on how they are counted. Together they make up a large part of body weight.
roughly how many watts of power does you: The brain runs on about 12 to 20 watts, which is similar to a dim light bulb, even though it uses around 20% of the body's energy. It is more energy-efficient than any computer of comparable power.
according to a study published in the an: Studies, including one reported in the Annals of Neurology, have found that people regularly exposed to certain pesticides have a higher risk of Parkinson's disease. Researchers think the chemicals may damage dopamine-producing neurons.
this medical term refers to a decrease i: Leukopenia is a lower-than-normal number of white blood cells (leukocytes), which can make infections more likely. It can be caused by infections, certain drugs or bone marrow problems.
although minimal, the risk of transmitti: Unsterilized tattoo needles or equipment can spread blood-borne infections like hepatitis B and C. That's why a clean, licensed studio using single-use needles is important.
which blood constituent is involved in t: Platelets, the blood cells that help form clots, can be stored for only about 5 to 7 days, so blood banks need regular donors. They're kept at room temperature and gently agitated.
there is no cure for this disease that i: Muscular dystrophy is a group of inherited diseases that gradually weaken muscles, and there is no cure, though treatments can help manage symptoms. A muscle biopsy can show the characteristic changes.
the framingham heart study concluded tha: The Framingham Heart Study found lower coronary heart disease risk in moderate drinkers than in non-drinkers, but heavy drinking raises the risk of many other health problems. More recent research questions whether alcohol has any benefit.
this agent, present in the skin of grape: Resveratrol is a compound found in grape skins, especially red grapes, and in red wine. It has antioxidant properties, but its health benefits in humans are still being studied.
this oil is said to be the richest natur: Wheat germ oil is one of the richest natural sources of vitamin E, an antioxidant that is widely used in skincare products. It can also go rancid quickly.
this nut is also a source of folic acid,: Hazelnuts contain folate (vitamin B9) as well as vitamin E and healthy fats. They are the nut famously paired with chocolate, as in Nutella.
age-related macular degeneration, cancer: Spinach has folate, lutein, vitamin K and iron. Lutein is linked to a lower risk of age-related macular degeneration, and folate helps prevent neural tube defects.
this is one of the few non-fish oils tha: Soybean oil is a plant source of alpha-linolenic acid, an omega-3 fatty acid, and as a plant oil it contains no cholesterol. It is widely used in cooking and food products.
this ingredient is used in a lot of cosm: Pearl powder, made from ground cultured pearls, has been used in Asian cosmetics and traditional medicine for centuries. Claims that it keeps skin young are mostly traditional, not proven.
these substances are added to lotions an: Emollients are moisturizing ingredients that soften and smooth the skin by filling gaps between skin cells. Examples are petroleum jelly, shea butter and glycerin.
the active ingredient of absinthe is thu: Thujone is a compound in wormwood, the herb in absinthe. Contrary to old claims, absinthe doesn't cause hallucinations, and its strong effects come mainly from its very high alcohol content.
common sage, also known as garden sage,: Some small studies suggest sage extract may help memory and thinking in mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease, but it's not an established treatment. People should check with a doctor before using herbal remedies.
this deciduous tree, popular as maidenha: Ginkgo biloba, also called the maidenhair tree, is a "living fossil" that has existed for about 200 million years. Many people take it for memory, but studies haven't shown strong benefits.
this blood alcohol content level is gene: All US states now use a blood alcohol content of 0.08% as the legal limit for drivers over 21, and the older 0.10% limit was gradually lowered. Lower limits apply to commercial drivers and drivers under 21.
tsaritsa alexandra of russia called on g: Alexei, the son of Tsar Nicholas II and Tsarina Alexandra, had hemophilia, a disorder in which blood doesn't clot properly. The family turned to the mystic Rasputin, whose influence at court became a scandal.
what is the name of the american who pat: Paul Winchell, a ventriloquist and inventor best known as the voice of Tigger, patented an artificial heart in 1963. He later donated the patent to the University of Utah, where artificial heart research continued.
the earliest recorded vaccination in his: People practiced inoculation against smallpox long before modern vaccines, using material from sufferers. Edward Jenner then developed the cowpox-based vaccine in 1796, which led to the eradication of smallpox in 1980.
the acronym we now use for this disease: AIDS, or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, got that name in 1982, when it replaced the earlier label GRID. The cause, HIV, was identified in 1983.
studies have found that coffee may reduc: Large studies have found that people who drink coffee regularly have a lower risk of Parkinson's disease. Researchers think caffeine may protect brain cells, but that doesn't prove cause and effect.
fainting is a loss of consciousness due: Syncope is the medical term for fainting, a temporary loss of consciousness caused by too little blood flow to the brain. It's often harmless but can sometimes signal a heart problem.
one version of this rare brain disorder: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) is a rare, fatal brain disease caused by prions. A variant form is linked to eating beef from cattle with "mad cow disease" (BSE).
people diagnosed with this disease have: Pica is a condition in which people crave and eat things that aren't food, such as dirt, chalk, paper or clay. It can be linked to iron deficiency, pregnancy or mental health conditions.
this progressive generative disease of t: Huntington's disease is an inherited brain disorder that causes uncontrolled movements called chorea, from the Greek word for "dance", as well as mental decline. It is caused by a faulty gene on chromosome 4.
this disorder is the abnormal accumulati: Hydrocephalus, meaning "water on the brain", is a buildup of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain's ventricles. A shunt is often placed to drain the extra fluid.
what medical term is synonym of jaundice: Icterus is the medical word for jaundice, from the Greek "ikteros". The yellow color comes from a buildup of bilirubin.
at this stage of the plague, one of the: In septicemic plague, the infection spreads in the blood and can turn skin black from tissue death. This is one reason the medieval pandemic was called the "Black Death".
located in the upper anterior portion of: The thymus, located behind the breastbone, is part of the lymphatic and immune systems and is where T cells mature. It is large in children and shrinks after puberty.
this extremely vital nerve is responsibl: The vagus nerve, the 10th cranial nerve, runs from the brainstem to the abdomen and controls the heart rate, digestion and parts of speech and swallowing. Its name comes from the Latin for "wandering".
the human facial skull consists of doubl: The calcaneus is the heel bone in the foot, not a bone of the face. The facial skeleton includes bones such as the maxilla, mandible, nasal bones and zygomatic (cheek) bones.
this physician has been trained in the d: A nephrologist is a doctor who specializes in the kidneys and treats conditions such as kidney failure and kidney stones. The name comes from the Greek "nephros", meaning kidney.
which one of the following medications t: Aricept (donepezil) is a drug used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease. It slows the breakdown of acetylcholine in the brain but doesn't cure the disease.
which of the following drugs thins the b: Coumadin (warfarin) is a blood thinner that makes it harder for blood to clot, which is used to prevent strokes and clots. It works by blocking vitamin K, so patients need to watch their intake of vitamin K foods.
cavities are generally painless. however: Tooth decay starts in the enamel and then reaches the dentin, a softer layer containing tiny nerve channels. By the time it reaches the dentin, cavities often start to hurt.
which type of blood cells can be stored: Red blood cells can be stored refrigerated for about 42 days, while platelets last only 5 to 7 days. Plasma can be frozen and stored for up to a year.
an ancient chinese book called the inner: The Huangdi Neijing, or Inner Canon of the Yellow Emperor, is attributed to the legendary Yellow Emperor, though it was probably compiled over several centuries around the 2nd century BC. It is a foundation of traditional Chinese medicine.
which of the following types of brain ce: Glial cells, such as astrocytes, support and protect neurons, maintain the brain's chemical balance and help signals travel. There are about as many of them as neurons.
which of the following is not part of th: The circle of Willis is a ring of arteries at the base of the brain that includes the anterior and posterior cerebral arteries and the communicating arteries. The basilar artery feeds into it but isn't part of the circle itself.
this scientist, winner of the 1908 nobel: Paul Ehrlich, who shared the 1908 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, noticed that dyes injected into the blood stained most organs but not the brain. This led to the idea of the blood-brain barrier.
this pollutant causes inflammation of th: Smog contains ground-level ozone and fine particles that irritate the lungs, causing coughing, chest pain and reduced lung function. Long-term exposure can permanently harm lung tissue.
substance vital for treating what heredi: Hemophilia, which mostly affects males, is treated with clotting factors such as factor VIII, which are now made using genetic engineering. This is safer than using factors taken from donated blood.
which skeletal muscle is used in blowing: The buccinator, a cheek muscle, is used for blowing, whistling and smiling. It's sometimes called the "trumpeter's muscle" because it helps trumpeters hold air.
which skeletal muscle raises or throws b: The trapezius is a large, triangular muscle across the upper back and neck that raises the shoulders and helps hold the head up. It's named for its trapezoid shape.
which skeletal muscle extends the foot,: The gastrocnemius, the main calf muscle, points the foot down and lets you stand on tiptoes. It works with the deeper soleus muscle.
in what part of the human body are the w: Wormian bones are small extra bones found in the sutures, or joints, of the skull. They're named after Ole Worm, a Danish physician, and are common in some conditions.
what nervous system ailment, characteriz: Beriberi is caused by a lack of vitamin B1 (thiamine), and it affects the nerves and heart. It was common where people lived mostly on polished white rice.
this mental illness, classified by emil: Schizophrenia is a serious mental illness involving delusions, hallucinations and disorganized thinking. Emil Kraepelin described it in the 1880s as "dementia praecox", and Eugen Bleuler coined the name "schizophrenia" in 1908.
which medical term refers to the crackli: Crepitus is the crackling or popping sound heard or felt when rough surfaces rub together, like bone ends or in a joint. Cracking knuckles is a common, usually harmless, example.
when you take a shower or bath for a lon: Wrinkled fingers in the bath aren't just from soaking up water; research suggests the nervous system causes blood vessels in the fingertips to narrow. Wet, wrinkled fingers may give a better grip on slippery objects.
this mineral, an important component of: Phosphorus, mostly as calcium phosphate, makes up a major part of bones and teeth, and it's also found in cell membranes and DNA. It's found in dairy, meat and nuts.
which tree, that grows on the canary isl: The dragon tree (Dracaena draco) grows in the Canary Islands, Cape Verde and Madeira, and its red resin is known as "dragon's blood". It has been used as a dye and medicine since ancient times.
what fruit is believed to be the highest: The Kakadu plum, an Australian fruit also called gubinge, is believed to have the highest vitamin C content of any fruit, up to about 100 times that of oranges. Indigenous Australians have long used it as food and medicine.
what term means fear of skin diseases?: Dermatosiophobia is the fear of skin diseases. Phobias are named by combining a Greek word with "phobia", which means fear.
a wax sculpture at the london madame tus: William S. Burroughs, author of Naked Lunch, accidentally shot and killed his wife, Joan Vollmer, in Mexico City in 1951 while playing a "William Tell" game. He was never tried for it and later said it shaped his writing.
it is the magical power of this herb: in: Angelica, the "herb of angels", was believed in medieval Europe to ward off evil and protect against plague. Its stalks are still used in cooking and candied.
when the arm is bent in the elbow joint: The deltoid is the thick, triangular muscle over the shoulder that raises the arm to the side (abducts it). It gives the shoulder its rounded shape.
pathogenic microorganisms which get into: Antibodies are made by B lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell. When they recognize an antigen, they develop into plasma cells that produce large numbers of antibodies.
in 1658 he became the first person to de: Dutch scientist Jan Swammerdam was the first to observe red blood cells with a microscope in 1658. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek later described them in more detail.
bone surfaces are not featureless and sm: A trochanter is a large, blunt projection on a bone, like those at the top of the femur where muscles attach. The femur has a greater and a lesser trochanter.
this disease is characterized by the pre: Ménière's disease is an inner-ear disorder causing vertigo attacks, hearing loss, ringing in the ears (tinnitus) and a feeling of fullness. It was named for the French physician Prosper Ménière, who described it in 1861.
